subject: Evaluation decision matrix, deployment gates & acceptance test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearhealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation decision matrix, deployment gates & acceptance test plan

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. Per our conversation, I drafted a concise mutual action plan (attached) that turns the MAP into a clear set of evaluation milestones, required evidence artifacts, and the exit gates we expect to validate before a production go/no-go. The goal is to keep the pilot tight (30 days) and make acceptance objective so procurement and engineering can sign off quickly.

High-level asks in the attached MAP-v1:
- Week 1: Integration smoke (API connectivity, auth, test corpus ingestion) — evidence: connectivity logs, sample responses (3 endpoints)
- Week 2: Latency & throughput baseline (90th pct < 450ms for typical queries) — evidence: perf traces and token-level breakdown
- Week 3: Quality spot checks (closed set accuracy and concordance) — evidence: eval reports + top 20 failure cases
- Week 4: Cutover rehearsal & rollback plan — evidence: runbook and one rollback drill documented

Can you confirm these milestones map to ClearHealth's success criteria, and whether procurement needs additional language around data retention or audit evidence? If OK, Ben and Karthik will attach SLA/rollback wording and owners.

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)], [Attachment: evidence-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearhealth.com
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation decision matrix, deployment gates & acceptance test plan

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear MAP. This format helps a lot. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock timelines:
1) Week 2 perf target — our infra team will run load with a subset of production traffic; can you confirm the test harness and a preferred replay window?
2) Data retention: we need explicit confirmation that request/response traces for customer PII will be redacted in evidence exports. Is that supported for the pilot?
3) Procurement: please include a short description of the audit artifacts we will receive (SOC2 logs, access logs) and a draft retention schedule.

We are generally aligned with the 30-day slice but may ask for a 7-day buffer at the end for compliance sign-off. Procurement looped in.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Director, Data Platform
ClearHealth
Samantha.Lee@clearhealth.com

Subject: Re: Evaluation decision matrix, deployment gates & acceptance test plan

Thanks Samantha — good questions. Short answers below, and I've updated the MAP (see v1.1 notes in the workbook).

1) Test harness & replay — we can provide the Redwood test harness (Docker image + replay config). Recommended replay window: 1 hour of representative traffic streamed at target QPS. We'll coordinate a slot with your infra team; Karthik will own the replay orchestration.

2) PII redaction — supported. For the pilot evidence exports we will redact sensitive fields by default and provide a redaction report that highlights what was removed. If you need unredacted traces for legal review, that can be handled under bilateral NDA and a controlled access workflow.

3) Audit artifacts & retention — Ben attached a short artifact list below (SOC2 summary, access logs, audit trail). Retention: we typically provide 90 days of detailed logs and a 12-month aggregated report; we can extend per contract.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Monday: infra sync to schedule replay (owner: karthik_iyer)
- Tuesday: procurement review of artifact list and retention (owner: procurement@clearhealth.com)
- Wednesday: run first integration smoke and share connectivity logs (owner: marissa_cole)

If that looks right I'll convert the MAP sheet to a shared doc and update owners.

Best,
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation decision matrix, deployment gates & acceptance test plan

Adding a few operational constraints and acceptance mechanics so procurement has something concrete:

- SLA/rollback language: propose a pilot-level SLA target (p99 endpoint latency < 800ms) and a canary rollback trigger (error rate > 2% sustained for 10 minutes) — samples included in the attachment.
- Evidence packaging: we will deliver a zip with the following named artifacts per gate: connectivity_logs.zip, perf_traces.json, eval_report.html, and a signed redaction_report.txt.
- Test owners: name owners on each gate in the MAP sheet (Karthik = replay/operator, Marissa = customer comms, Ben = evidence curator).

I've attached the SLA snippet and a one-page acceptance checklist for your procurement team to review.

[Attachment: pilot-sla-snippet.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Evaluation decision matrix, deployment gates & acceptance test plan

Marissa, Ben —

This is great — procurement reviewed the artifact list and the SLA snippet and asked only for one minor tweak on retention language (extend detailed logs to 180 days for archived evidence; we'll include this in a short amendment). Otherwise procurement is happy with the acceptance checklist.

Operationally we confirm:
- Monday 08:00 PT: infra replay slot (Karthik to coordinate)
- Wed 09:00 PT: integration smoke (Marissa owner)
- Week 3: quality spot checks (we will provide evaluation prompts and agree on pass thresholds)

Please convert MAP-v1.1 into a shared Google Sheet with owners and dates filled and send a final copy. After the integration smoke we'll schedule a 30-minute sign-off call to confirm go/no-go criteria.

Thanks for being rigorous here — the objective acceptance plan makes procurement much more comfortable.

Best,
Samantha
